newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen's tourism revenues reach $41 million in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Yemen's tourism revenues reach $41 million in 1996.

text.p: Yemen's tourism revenue rose to $41 million in 1996, up from $38 million the previous year, an official statement said.
The statement, issued by the government's General Tourism Board and obtained by Reuters on Tuesday, said the number of foreign tourists to Yemen increased to 74,000 compared with 60,000 in 1995.

It said the country, nestled between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden at the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula, currently had 421 hotels and hostels with 6,000 rooms, 4,500 of which offered "reasonable services". It did not elaborate.

Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest countries, has recently suffered from a spate of tourist kidnappings by tribesman seeking to put pressure on the government. The hostages, mostly from Europe and the United States, have all been released unharmed.
